name: TokenRouter
desc: Built an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that converts between provider protocols, routes by priority and weight with failure-aware retries, and reserves and settles token quotas concurrency-safely.
highlights: Hardened relay and control planes with SSRF-safe outbound dialing, JWT refresh rotation with replay detection, Casbin RBAC, and WebAuthn/TOTP step-up verification; validated quota accounting under race-condition tests.
summary: One gateway for multiple AI providers, with secure routing and concurrency-safe token accounting.

caseStudy.problem: Applications need one gateway for different AI provider protocols, with usage accounting that stays consistent when requests overlap or fail.
caseStudy.decision: User and API-token quota holds are paired in one database transaction. Settlement and refunds are idempotent, and durable reservation records keep failed operations available for reconciliation.
caseStudy.evidence: The test suites cover atomic settlement, repeated settlement and refunds, rollback on failure, and concurrent reservations that cannot overspend.

flow.title: Accept the request
flow.description: An OpenAI-compatible client sends a request to the gateway.

flow.title: Reserve quota
flow.description: A database transaction holds the user and API-token quotas together.

flow.title: Route and translate
flow.description: Provider adapters translate protocols; routing uses priority, weight, and failure-aware retries.

flow.title: Settle or refund
flow.description: Actual usage settles the reservation; unused quota is released. Failed settlement remains available for reconciliation.

name: MobileID
desc: Built a Django/Vue identity platform for PDF417 barcode generation, profile management, and device-aware sessions on PostgreSQL and DynamoDB.
highlights: Layered authentication defenses: HTTP-only cookie JWTs, CSRF validation, refresh-token rotation and blacklisting, immediate session revocation, and Argon2 hashing.
Gated CI on Bandit, Safety, Trivy, and dependency audits at a 70% coverage floor, plus Playwright E2E suites and Docker/Vite build validation.
summary: A Django/Vue identity platform with barcode workflows and control over sessions on other devices.

caseStudy.problem: A mobile identity application needs barcode and profile workflows alongside control over authenticated sessions on other devices.
caseStudy.decision: Cookie-based JWT authentication combines refresh-token blacklisting with access-session revocation checks on subsequent API requests. Cookie-authenticated writes also require CSRF validation.
caseStudy.evidence: Tests cover device listing, revoking one or all other devices, rejection of revoked access tokens, and CSRF enforcement. CI configures a 70% backend coverage floor alongside security checks and Playwright suites.

flow.title: Choose a device
flow.description: The signed-in user selects a device from their session list.

flow.title: Revoke session state
flow.description: The Django API revokes the selected session and blacklists its refresh token.

flow.title: Check the next request
flow.description: API authentication checks the access token against revoked session state.

flow.title: Reject revoked access
flow.description: The revoked session cannot continue using that access token or refresh it.
